title: The smoothest average and some extremal problems for polynomials
summary: We study the problem of finding the "smoothest'' local average of a function $f \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$ when we consider its convolution with suitable kernels $u$. The measurement of smoothness is as follows: Given a positive integer $k$, we aim to minimize the constant \begin{equation*} \sup_{0 \neq f \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z})} \frac{\|\nabla^{k}(u\ast f)\|_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})}}{\|f\|_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})}} \end{equation*} among all symmetric kernels $u : \{-n,\dots,n\} \to \mathbb{R}$ with normalization $\sum_{j=-n}^{n}u(j) = 1$.
